title: Right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and bidi reordering
stressor: right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) and bidi reordering with embedded LTR
notes: Arabic and Hebrew paragraphs use dir="rtl"; the mixed line embeds Latin (Nyala, RTL) and digits (1024) inside Arabic to exercise bidi reordering. Fonts are subset from Noto faces shipped with mullvad-browser in the Nix store (NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf, NotoSansHebrew-Regular.ttf, both OFL-1.1), subset with pyftsubset to only the sample glyphs, output as woff (zlib; woff2 unavailable, no brotli python ext), and base64-embedded in @font-face. Glyphs were confirmed to render as real Arabic/Hebrew script (no tofu boxes) in the captured screenshot.png. The embedded fonts make rendering deterministic and independent of system Arabic/Hebrew fonts.

placement_gate.reason: Arabic shaped-cluster advances exceed the forced monospace advance; Latin runs on this page score 0.000, and a new drifted box still trips the pinned count. At the 240x48 wide leg the 1280 CSS-pixel reflow packs the Arabic run and the embedded LTR run one cell tighter, so the shaped bidi runs overlap by one same-row cell (collisions 1).
